mishnayos.summary: A korban that was shechted with a different korban in mind is still kosher, but it does not count for the owner. A korban Pesach and a chatas become pasul this way, and Rabbi Eliezer says an asham does too.

chunks.en: All korbanos that were shechted for the wrong purpose,
chunks.st: All slaughtered offerings that were slaughtered not for their own sake,
chunks.stMore: i.e., during the slaughtering the slaughterer’s intent was to sacrifice a different offering,

words.note: Shechted while thinking of a different kind of korban.

chunks.he: כְּשֵׁרִים, אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא עָלוּ לַבְּעָלִים לְשֵׁם חוֹבָה.
chunks.en: are kosher, but they do not count for the owner's duty.
chunks.st: are fit, and one may continue their sacrificial rites and partake of their meat where that applies. But these offerings did not satisfy the obligation of the owner, who is therefore required to bring another offering.

words.note: Literally "go up."

chunks.en: Except for the korban Pesach and the chatas.
chunks.st: This is the halakha with regard to all offerings except for the Paschal offering and the sin offering.
chunks.stMore: In those cases, if the owner sacrificed them not for their own sake, they are unfit. But there is a difference between the two exceptions.

words.note: A korban brought for a sin done by mistake.

chunks.en: The korban Pesach is pasul only at its own time,
chunks.st: The Paschal offering is unfit only when sacrificed not for its sake at its appointed time, on the fourteenth day of Nisan after noon,

words.note: The fourteenth of Nisan, after midday.

chunks.en: and the chatas at any time.
chunks.st: while the sin offering is unfit any time that it is sacrificed not for its sake.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: also the asham.
chunks.st: The guilt offering too
chunks.stMore: is unfit when sacrificed not for its sake. According to his opinion, the correct reading of the mishna is:

words.note: A korban brought to fix certain sins.

chunks.en: So the korban Pesach is pasul at its own time,
chunks.st: The Paschal offering is unfit only at its appointed time,

chunks.en: and the chatas and the asham
chunks.st: while the sin offering and the guilt offering

chunks.en: at any time.
chunks.st: are unfit at all times.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer said:
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer said in explanation:

chunks.en: The chatas comes for a sin,
chunks.st: The sin offering is brought for performance of a transgression

chunks.en: and the asham comes for a sin.
chunks.st: and the guilt offering is brought for performance of a transgression.

chunks.en: Just as a chatas is pasul when it is not for its own sake,
chunks.st: Just as a sin offering is unfit when sacrificed not for its sake,

words.note: Not kosher.

chunks.en: so too an asham is pasul when it is not for its own sake.
chunks.st: so too, the guilt offering is unfit when sacrificed not for its sake.

mishnayos.summary: Some Rabbis add more rules about a korban shechted for the wrong purpose. Shimon, brother of Azarya, says: if it was shechted for a holier korban it is kosher, but for a less holy korban it is pasul.

chunks.en: Yosei ben Choni says,
chunks.st: Yosei ben Ḥoni says:
chunks.stMore: Not only are the Paschal offering and the sin offering unfit when slaughtered not for their sake,

chunks.en: korbanos shechted for the sake of a Pesach or a chatas
chunks.st: but also other offerings that are slaughtered for the sake of a Paschal offering and for the sake of a sin offering

chunks.en: are pasul. Shimon, the brother of Azarya, says:
chunks.st: are unfit. Shimon, brother of Azarya, says that this is the distinction: With regard to all offerings,

chunks.en: If he shechted them for a korban holier than they are,
chunks.st: if one slaughtered them for the sake of an offering whose level of sanctity is greater than theirs,

chunks.en: they are kosher. For a korban less holy than they are,
chunks.st: they are fit; if one slaughtered them for the sake of an offering whose level of sanctity is less than theirs,

chunks.en: they are pasul. How so?
chunks.st: they are unfit. How so?

chunks.he: קָדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים שֶׁשְּׁחָטָן לְשֵׁם קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים,
chunks.en: The holiest korbanos, shechted for the sake of less holy korbanos,
chunks.st: Offerings of the most sacred order, e.g., sin offerings and burnt offerings, that one slaughtered for the sake of offerings of lesser sanctity, e.g., peace offerings,

words.note: Like the olah and the chatas.
Like the shelamim.

chunks.he: פְּסוּלִין. קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים שֶׁשְּׁחָטָן לְשֵׁם קָדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים,
chunks.en: are pasul. Less holy korbanos shechted for the holiest korbanos
chunks.st: are unfit. Offerings of lesser sanctity that one slaughtered for the sake of offerings of the most sacred order

chunks.he: כְּשֵׁרִין. הַבְּכוֹר וְהַמַּעֲשֵׂר שֶׁשְּׁחָטָן לְשֵׁם שְׁלָמִים,
chunks.en: are kosher. A bechor or maaser shechted for a shelamim
chunks.st: are fit. Likewise, there is a distinction between different offerings of lesser sanctity. The firstborn animal and the animal tithe that one slaughtered for the sake of a peace offering

words.note: A firstborn animal, given to the Kohen.
Every tenth animal, set aside as holy.
A korban that the owner shares in eating.

chunks.en: are kosher. But a shelamim shechted for a bechor
chunks.st: are fit, as the sanctity of peace offerings is greater. Peace offerings that one slaughtered for the sake of a firstborn

chunks.en: or for maaser is pasul.
chunks.st: animal or for the sake of an animal tithe are unfit.

mishnayos.summary: A korban Pesach shechted for the wrong purpose on the morning of the fourteenth of Nisan: Rabbi Yehoshua says it is kosher and Ben Beseira says it is pasul. Ben Azzai shares a tradition from seventy-two elders.

chunks.en: A korban Pesach that he shechted on the morning of the fourteenth
chunks.st: With regard to the Paschal offering that one slaughtered on the morning of the fourteenth
chunks.stMore: of Nisan, the day when the Paschal offering should be slaughtered in the afternoon,

chunks.en: not for its own sake,
chunks.st: if he did so not for its sake,

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says it is kosher,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua deems it fit

chunks.en: as if it was shechted on the thirteenth.
chunks.st: as though it were slaughtered on the thirteenth
chunks.stMore: of Nisan. An animal consecrated as a Paschal offering that was slaughtered not at its designated time for the sake of a different offering is fit for sacrifice as a peace offering.

chunks.en: Ben Beseira says it is pasul,
chunks.st: Ben Beteira deems it unfit

chunks.en: as if it was shechted in the afternoon.
chunks.st: as though it were slaughtered in the afternoon of the fourteenth.

words.note: The afternoon, the right time for shechting the korban Pesach.

chunks.en: Shimon ben Azzai said,
chunks.st: Shimon ben Azzai said:

chunks.he: מְקֻבָּל אֲנִי מִפִּי שִׁבְעִים וּשְׁנַיִם זָקֵן,
chunks.en: I have a tradition from seventy-two elders,
chunks.st: I received a tradition from seventy-two elders,

words.note: Wise Rabbis of the Sanhedrin.

chunks.en: on the day they seated Rabbi Elazar
chunks.st: as the Sanhedrin deliberated and decided on the day that they installed Rabbi Elazar

chunks.en: ben Azarya as head of the yeshivah,
chunks.st: ben Azarya at the head of the yeshiva

chunks.he: שֶׁכָּל הַזְּבָחִים הַנֶּאֱכָלִים שֶׁנִּזְבְּחוּ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָן,
chunks.en: that all korbanos that are eaten, if shechted for the wrong purpose,
chunks.st: and ruled that all the slaughtered offerings that are eaten that were slaughtered not for their sake

chunks.he: כְּשֵׁרִים, אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא עָלוּ לַבְּעָלִים מִשּׁוּם חוֹבָה,
chunks.en: are kosher, but they do not count for the owner's duty,
chunks.st: are fit, but these offerings did not satisfy the obligation of the owner,

chunks.en: except for the korban Pesach and the chatas.
chunks.st: except for the Paschal offering and the sin offering. Based on that version,

chunks.he: וְלֹא הוֹסִיף בֶּן עַזַּאי אֶלָּא הָעוֹלָה,
chunks.en: Ben Azzai added only the olah,
chunks.st: ben Azzai added to the halakha cited in the first mishna only the burnt offering, which is not eaten,

words.note: A korban burned whole on the mizbeach.

chunks.en: and the Sages did not agree with him.
chunks.st: and the Rabbis disagreed and did not concede to him.

mishnayos.summary: A korban Pesach or chatas becomes pasul if any of its four main jobs is done with the wrong purpose in mind. Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi Eliezer argue about carrying the blood to the mizbeach.

chunks.en: A korban Pesach or chatas that he shechted for the wrong purpose,
chunks.st: With regard to the Paschal offering and the sin offering, where one slaughtered them not for their sake,

chunks.en: or he caught the blood, or carried it,
chunks.st: or where he collected their blood in a vessel, conveyed this blood to the altar,

chunks.en: or threw it, for the wrong purpose,
chunks.st: or sprinkled this blood on the altar not for their sake,

chunks.en: or for their sake and then not for their sake,
chunks.st: or where he performed one of these sacrificial rites for their sake and not for their sake,

chunks.en: or not for their sake and then for their sake,
chunks.st: or not for their sake and for their sake,

chunks.en: they are pasul. What is for their sake and not for their sake?
chunks.st: in all these cases the offerings are unfit. How are these rites performed for their sake and not for their sake?

chunks.en: For the sake of a Pesach and for the sake of a shelamim.
chunks.st: In a case where one slaughtered the Paschal offering for the sake of a Paschal offering and for the sake of a peace offering.

chunks.en: And not for their sake and then for their sake?
chunks.st: How are these rites performed not for their sake and for their sake?

chunks.en: For the sake of a shelamim and for the sake of a Pesach.
chunks.st: In a case where one slaughtered the Paschal offering for the sake of a peace offering and for the sake of a Paschal offering.

chunks.en: Because a korban can become pasul in four jobs:
chunks.st: The offering is unfit because a slaughtered offering is disqualified due to prohibited intent in four matters:

chunks.en: shechting, catching the blood, carrying it, and throwing it.
chunks.st: In the performance of the sacrificial rites of slaughtering the animal, in collecting the blood, in conveying the blood, and in sprinkling the blood.

words.note: On the mizbeach.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says it stays kosher if it happened while carrying,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon deems the offering fit if the prohibited intent was during the rite of conveying the blood,

chunks.en: because Rabbi Shimon used to say,
chunks.st: as he would say:

chunks.en: It is impossible without shechting,
chunks.st: It is impossible to sacrifice an offering without slaughtering the animal,

chunks.en: or without catching the blood or throwing it,
chunks.st: or without collection of the blood, or without sprinkling the blood,

chunks.en: but it is possible without carrying it.
chunks.st: but it is possible to sacrifice an offering without conveying the blood to the altar. How so?

chunks.en: He can shecht next to the mizbeach and throw.
chunks.st: If one slaughters the animal alongside the altar and sprinkles
chunks.stMore: the blood, the blood does not need to be conveyed. Therefore, the rite of conveying the blood is not significant enough to cause the offering to be disqualified due to prohibited intent while performing it.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: If he carries where he needs to carry it,
chunks.st: With regard to one who conveys the blood in a situation where he is required to convey it,

chunks.en: the wrong thought makes it pasul.
chunks.st: prohibited intent while conveying it disqualifies the offering.

chunks.en: But where he does not need to carry it,
chunks.st: If he conveys the blood in a situation where he is not required to convey it,

chunks.en: the wrong thought does not make it pasul.
chunks.st: prohibited intent while conveying it does not disqualify the offering.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah lists people who make a korban pasul if they catch its blood, and wrong ways of putting the blood on the mizbeach. In these cases the korban is pasul, but there is no kares for eating it.

chunks.en: All korbanos whose blood was caught by a non-Kohen,
chunks.st: With regard to all slaughtered offerings, if the one who collected their blood was a non-priest;

words.note: Someone who is not a Kohen.

chunks.en: or by a Kohen in mourning, or one who toveled today,
chunks.st: or a priest who was an acute mourner, i.e., one whose relative has died and has not yet been buried; or one who was ritually impure who immersed that day
chunks.stMore: and is waiting for nightfall for the purification process to be completed;

words.note: A Kohen whose close relative died and is not yet buried.
He went to the mikvah today and becomes tahor only at night.

chunks.en: or a Kohen missing his special clothes, or one who still has to bring his korban to finish becoming tahor,
chunks.st: or one who has not yet brought an atonement offering, e.g., a zav or leper after the seventh day of the purification process; or a priest lacking the requisite priestly vestments;

words.note: The special clothes a Kohen wears for the avodah.
He still has to bring a korban to finish becoming tahor.

chunks.en: or one who did not wash his hands and feet,
chunks.st: or one who did not wash his hands and feet
chunks.stMore: from the water in the Basin prior to performing the Temple service;

chunks.en: or a Kohen without a bris, or one who is tamei,
chunks.st: or an uncircumcised priest; or a ritually impure priest;

chunks.en: or one sitting, or standing on top of vessels,
chunks.st: or if the one who collected the blood was sitting; or if he was standing not on the floor of the Temple but upon vessels,

chunks.en: or on top of an animal,
chunks.st: or upon an animal,

chunks.en: or on top of his friend's feet,
chunks.st: or upon the feet of another,

chunks.en: made it pasul. If he caught the blood with his left hand,
chunks.st: he has disqualified the offering. If he collected the blood with his left hand,

chunks.en: he made it pasul. Rabbi Shimon says it is kosher.
chunks.st: he disqualified the blood for offering. In this last case, Rabbi Shimon deems it fit.

chunks.en: If the blood spilled on the floor and he gathered it up,
chunks.st: If the blood spilled on the floor before the priest managed to collect it into a vessel, and the priest then collected it from the floor into a vessel,

chunks.en: it is pasul. If he put the blood on the ramp,
chunks.st: it is disqualified. If the priest placed the blood upon the ramp leading up to the altar,

words.note: The ramp the Kohanim walked up to reach the top of the mizbeach.

chunks.en: or on a part of the mizbeach that is not over its base,
chunks.st: or if he placed it on the wall of the altar in an area that is not opposite the base
chunks.stMore: of the altar, i.e., in those parts of the altar where there is no foundation;

words.note: The bottom step of the mizbeach, which did not go all the way around.

chunks.en: or he put blood that goes below
chunks.st: or if he placed the blood that is to be placed below
chunks.stMore: the red line that runs along the middle of the altar, e.g., the blood of a burnt offering,

words.note: Below the red line around the middle of the mizbeach.

chunks.en: above, or blood that goes above,
chunks.st: above the red line, or if he placed the blood that is to be placed above the red line, e.g., the blood of a sin offering,

chunks.en: below; or blood that goes inside,
chunks.st: below the red line; or if he placed the blood that is to be placed inside
chunks.stMore: the Sanctuary, i.e., on the golden altar or in the Holy of Holies,

words.note: Inside the Heichal, on the golden mizbeach or in the Kodesh HaKodashim.

chunks.en: outside; or blood that goes outside,
chunks.st: outside the Sanctuary on the external altar, or if he placed the blood that is to be placed outside

chunks.en: inside, it is pasul, but there is no kares.
chunks.st: the Sanctuary inside the Sanctuary, in all these cases the offering is disqualified. Nevertheless, there is no liability for karet for one who partakes of these offerings.

words.note: A punishment from Heaven for very serious sins.

mishnayos.summary: If someone shechts a korban planning to do its jobs outside the Beis HaMikdash, it is pasul. If he plans to do them the next day, after their time, it becomes piggul, and one who eats it gets kares.

chunks.en: One who shechts the korban planning to throw its blood
chunks.st: With regard to one who slaughters the offering with intent to sprinkle its blood

chunks.en: outside, or some of its blood outside,
chunks.st: outside the Temple or to sprinkle part of its blood outside the Temple,

words.note: Outside the courtyard of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: to burn its parts for the mizbeach outside,
chunks.st: to burn its sacrificial portions outside

words.note: The fats and parts of the korban burned on the mizbeach.

chunks.en: or some of those parts outside,
chunks.st: the Temple or to burn part of its sacrificial portions outside the Temple,

chunks.en: to eat its meat outside, or an olive-size
chunks.st: to partake of its meat outside the Temple or to partake of an olive-bulk

chunks.en: of its meat outside, or to eat an olive-size
chunks.st: of its meat outside the Temple, or to partake of an olive-bulk

chunks.en: of the skin of the tail outside,
chunks.st: of the skin of the tail outside the Temple,

words.note: The fatty tail of a sheep.

chunks.en: it is pasul, but there is no kares.
chunks.st: in all of these cases the offering is disqualified, and there is no liability for karet for one who partakes of it.

chunks.en: If he planned to throw its blood tomorrow, or
chunks.st: But if one had intent to sprinkle its blood the next day

chunks.en: some of its blood tomorrow,
chunks.st: or part of its blood the next day,

chunks.en: to burn its parts for the mizbeach tomorrow, or
chunks.st: to burn its sacrificial portions the next day or

chunks.en: some of those parts tomorrow,
chunks.st: to burn part of its sacrificial portions the next day,

chunks.he: לֶאֱכֹל בְּשָׂרוֹ לְמָחָר אוֹ כַזַּיִת מִבְּשָׂרוֹ
chunks.en: to eat its meat tomorrow, or an olive-size of its meat
chunks.st: to partake of its meat the next day or to partake of an olive-bulk of its meat

chunks.he: לְמָחָר אוֹ כַּזַּיִת מֵעוֹר הָאַלְיָה לְמָחָר,
chunks.en: tomorrow, or an olive-size of the skin of the tail tomorrow,
chunks.st: the next day, or to partake of an olive-bulk of the skin of the tail the next day,

chunks.en: it is piggul, and one who eats it gets kares.
chunks.st: the offering is piggul, and one is liable to receive karet for burning or partaking of it.

words.note: A korban ruined by planning to eat or offer it after its time.

mishnayos.summary: The rule: if he plans, during one of the four jobs, to eat or burn the korban in the wrong place, it is pasul. If he plans to do it after its time, it is piggul, as long as everything else was done right.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle:

chunks.en: Anyone who shechts, catches the blood, carries it, or throws it,
chunks.st: With regard to anyone who slaughters the animal, or who collects the blood, or who conveys the blood, or who sprinkles the blood,

chunks.en: planning to eat something that is usually eaten,
chunks.st: with intent to partake of an item whose typical manner is such that one partakes of it, e.g., the meat of the offering,

chunks.en: or to burn something that is usually burned,
chunks.st: or to burn an item whose typical manner is such that one burns it on the altar,

chunks.en: outside its place,
chunks.st: if his intent was to partake of or to burn the measure of an olive-bulk outside its designated area,

chunks.en: it is pasul, but there is no kares.
chunks.st: the offering is disqualified, but there is no liability for karet for burning or partaking of it.

chunks.en: After its time,
chunks.st: If his intent was to do so beyond its designated time,

chunks.en: it is piggul, and one who eats it gets kares,
chunks.st: the offering is piggul and one is liable to receive karet for burning or partaking of it,

chunks.en: as long as the part that makes it allowed is offered the right way.
chunks.st: provided that the permitting factor, the blood, is sacrificed in accordance with its mitzva.

words.note: The blood, which makes the korban allowed once it is thrown.

mishnayos.summary: When is the blood "offered the right way" so the korban can become piggul? Only when the only wrong thought was about time. If there was also a thought about the wrong place, or the wrong purpose, it is not piggul.

chunks.en: How is the part that makes it allowed offered the right way?
chunks.st: How is the permitting factor sacrificed in accordance with its mitzva?

chunks.en: If he shechted without saying anything,
chunks.st: If one slaughtered the animal in silence with no specific intent,

words.note: With no special thought.

chunks.en: and caught, carried and threw the blood planning to eat it after its time;
chunks.st: and he collected and conveyed and sprinkled the blood with intent to burn or partake of the offering beyond its designated time;

chunks.en: or he shechted planning for after its time,
chunks.st: or if one slaughtered it with intent to burn or partake of the offering beyond its designated time,

chunks.en: and caught, carried and threw without saying anything;
chunks.st: and he collected and conveyed and sprinkled the blood in silence;

chunks.en: or he shechted,
chunks.st: or if one slaughtered

chunks.en: and caught, carried and threw, all planning for after its time,
chunks.st: the animal and collected and conveyed and sprinkled the blood with intent to burn or partake of the offering beyond its designated time,

chunks.en: that is when the part that makes it allowed is offered the right way.
chunks.st: that is the case where one sacrifices the permitting factor in accordance with its mitzva.

chunks.en: How is it not offered the right way?
chunks.st: How is the permitting factor not sacrificed in accordance with its mitzva?

chunks.en: If he shechted planning for outside its place,
chunks.st: If one slaughtered the animal with intent to burn it or partake of it outside its designated area,

chunks.en: and caught, carried and threw planning for after its time;
chunks.st: and he collected and conveyed and sprinkled the blood with intent to burn it or partake of it beyond its designated time;

chunks.en: or he shechted planning for after its time,
chunks.st: or if one slaughtered the animal with intent to burn it or partake of it beyond its designated time,

chunks.en: and caught, carried and threw planning for outside its place;
chunks.st: and collected and conveyed and sprinkled the blood with intent to burn it or partake of it outside its designated area;

chunks.en: or he shechted,
chunks.st: or if one slaughtered

chunks.en: caught, carried,
chunks.st: the animal and collected and conveyed

chunks.en: and threw, all planning for outside its place.
chunks.st: and sprinkled the blood with intent to burn it or partake of it outside its designated area,

chunks.en: Or a korban Pesach or chatas shechted for the wrong purpose,
chunks.st: in the case of the Paschal offering and the sin offering that one slaughtered not for their sake,

chunks.en: and he caught, carried and threw planning for after its time;
chunks.st: and one collected and conveyed and sprinkled the blood with intent to burn it or partake of it beyond its designated time;

chunks.en: or he shechted planning for after its time,
chunks.st: or if one slaughtered the Paschal offering or sin offering with intent to burn it or partake of it beyond its designated time,

chunks.en: and caught, carried and threw for the wrong purpose;
chunks.st: and he collected and conveyed and sprinkled the blood not for their sake;

chunks.en: or he shechted,
chunks.st: or that one slaughtered

chunks.en: caught, carried,
chunks.st: the Paschal offering or sin offering and collected and conveyed

chunks.en: and threw, all for the wrong purpose,
chunks.st: and sprinkled their blood not for their sake,

chunks.he: זֶה הוּא שֶׁלֹּא קָרַב הַמַּתִּיר כְּמִצְוָתוֹ:

mishnayos.summary: If he planned to eat some of the korban outside its place and some after its time, it is pasul but not piggul. Rabbi Yehudah says it depends on which thought came first. Eating and burning half-sizes do not add up.

chunks.en: If he planned to eat an olive-size outside and an olive-size tomorrow,
chunks.st: If one performed one of the sacrificial rites with the intent to eat an olive-bulk outside its designated area and an olive-bulk the next day,

chunks.stMore: e.g., the goats sacrificed for an unwitting communal sin of idol worship,

words.note: Special korbanos burned outside Yerushalayim instead of being eaten.

chunks.en: their blood makes their parts allowed to be offered.
chunks.st: their blood permits their sacrificial portions to be sacrificed on the altar.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:
chunks.stMore: Those bulls and goats are not subject to piggul because their blood is presented in the Sanctuary,

chunks.he: כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ עַל מִזְבֵּחַ הַחִיצוֹן כִּשְׁלָמִים,
chunks.en: anything whose blood is not on the outer mizbeach like a shelamim,
chunks.st: and in the case of any offering whose blood is not presented on the external altar like that of a peace offering,
chunks.stMore: with regard to which the halakha of piggul was stated in the Torah,

chunks.en: one is not punished for it because of piggul.
chunks.st: one is not liable for eating it due to violation of the prohibition of piggul.

mishnayos.summary: Korbanos of non-Jews cannot become piggul, nosar or tamei. Things that cannot become piggul can still become nosar or tamei, except the blood; Rabbi Shimon says that applies only to food.

chunks.en: Korbanos of non-Jews,
chunks.st: With regard to offerings consecrated by gentiles for sacrifice to God,

chunks.en: one is not punished for them because of piggul,
chunks.st: one is not liable for eating them, neither due to violation of the prohibition of piggul
chunks.stMore: if the sacrificial rites were performed with the intent to eat the offering beyond its designated time,

chunks.en: nosar, or tumah.
chunks.st: nor due to violation of the prohibition of notar, nor due to violation of the prohibition against eating the meat while ritually impure.

chunks.en: And one who shechts them outside
chunks.st: And one who slaughters them outside

words.note: Outside the courtyard of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: is not punished, says Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: the Temple courtyard is exempt; this is the statement of Rabbi Shimon.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says he is punished.
chunks.st: And Rabbi Yosei deems him liable.

chunks.he: דְּבָרִים שֶׁאֵין חַיָּבִין עֲלֵיהֶם מִשּׁוּם פִּגּוּל,
chunks.en: Things for which one is not punished because of piggul,
chunks.st: Even with regard to those items enumerated in the previous mishna (42b) for which one is not liable for eating them due to violation of the prohibition of piggul, e.g., the handful, the frankincense, and the incense,

chunks.en: one is punished for them because of nosar
chunks.st: one is, nevertheless, liable for eating them due to violation of the prohibition of notar,

chunks.en: and because of tumah,
chunks.st: and due to violation of the prohibition against eating consecrated food while ritually impure,

chunks.en: except for the blood.
chunks.st: except for the blood.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon deems one liable

chunks.en: only for something that is usually eaten.
chunks.st: for an item whose typical manner is such that one eats it.

chunks.en: But things like the wood, the levonah, and the ketores,
chunks.st: But with regard to the wood, the frankincense, and the incense,

chunks.en: one is not punished for them because of tumah.
chunks.st: one is not liable for eating them due to violation of the prohibition against eating a consecrated item while ritually impure.

mishnayos.summary: A korban is shechted with six things in mind, like the kind of korban, its owner and Hashem. Rabbi Yosei says it is kosher even without thinking of them, because Beis Din made a rule not to say any thought at all.

chunks.en: A korban is shechted for the sake of six things:
chunks.st: The slaughtered offering is slaughtered for the sake of six matters, and one must have all of these matters in mind:

chunks.en: for the sake of the korban,
chunks.st: For the sake of the particular type of offering being sacrificed;

chunks.en: for the sake of the one who brings it,
chunks.st: for the sake of the one who sacrifices the offering;

chunks.en: for the sake of Hashem,
chunks.st: for the sake of God;

chunks.en: for the sake of the fires of the mizbeach,
chunks.st: for the sake of consumption by the fires of the altar;

chunks.en: for the sake of the smell,
chunks.st: for the sake of the aroma;

chunks.en: for the sake of being pleasing to Hashem.
chunks.st: for the sake of the pleasing of God, i.e., in fulfillment of God’s will;

chunks.en: And the chatas and the asham,
chunks.st: and, in the cases of a sin offering and a guilt offering,

chunks.en: for the sake of the sin.
chunks.st: for the sake of atonement for the sin.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: even one who did not have in mind
chunks.st: Even in the case of one who did not have in mind

chunks.en: any one of all these,
chunks.st: to slaughter the offering for the sake of any one of these,

chunks.en: it is kosher, because this is a rule of Beis Din,
chunks.st: the offering is valid, as it is a stipulation of the court that he should not state any intent ab initio.

chunks.he: שֶׁאֵין הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה הוֹלֶכֶת אֶלָּא אַחַר הָעוֹבֵד:
chunks.en: since a thought goes only after the one doing the avodah.
chunks.st: This is necessary because the intent follows only the one performing the sacrificial rite,
chunks.stMore: and therefore if the one who slaughters the animal is not careful and states the wrong intent, the offering would be disqualified through his improper intent.

mishnayos.summary: This perek tells where each korban is shechted and eaten. The bull and goat of Yom Kippur are shechted in the north, and their blood is sprinkled in the Kodesh HaKodashim, on the paroches, and on the golden mizbeach.

chunks.en: Where is the place of the korbanos?
chunks.st: What is the location of the slaughtering and consumption of offerings?

chunks.en: The holiest korbanos are shechted in the north,
chunks.st: The principle is that with regard to offerings of the most sacred order, their slaughter is in the north of the Temple courtyard. Specifically,

words.note: The north side of the courtyard of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: The bull and the goat of the day
chunks.st: with regard to the bull and the goat of Yom Kippur,

chunks.en: of Yom Kippur are shechted in the north,
chunks.st: their slaughter is in the north

chunks.en: and their blood is caught in a holy vessel in the north,
chunks.st: and the collection of their blood in a service vessel is in the north,

words.note: A holy vessel used for the avodah.

chunks.he: וְדָמָן טָעוּן הַזָּיָה עַל בֵּין הַבַּדִּים
chunks.en: and their blood must be sprinkled between the poles
chunks.st: and their blood requires sprinkling between the staves of the Ark in the Holy of Holies,

words.note: The poles of the Aron in the Kodesh HaKodashim.

chunks.en: and on the paroches and on the golden mizbeach.
chunks.st: and upon the Curtain separating the Sanctuary and Holy of Holies, and on the golden altar. Concerning all those sprinklings,

words.note: The curtain in front of the Kodesh HaKodashim.

chunks.en: Each one of these puttings is a must.
chunks.st: failure to perform even one placement of their blood disqualifies the offering.

words.note: Without it the korban does not work.

chunks.en: The leftover blood he would pour on
chunks.st: As to the remainder of the blood, which is left after those sprinklings, a priest would pour

chunks.en: the western base of the outer mizbeach.
chunks.st: it onto the western base of the external altar.

chunks.en: If he did not put it there,
chunks.st: But if he did not place the remainder of the blood on the western base,

chunks.en: it does not hold it back.
chunks.st: it does not disqualify the offering.

mishnayos.summary: The bulls and goats that are burned are shechted in the north, and their blood is sprinkled on the paroches and the golden mizbeach. Afterwards they are burned outside the city, in the place of the ashes.

chunks.he: פָּרִים הַנִּשְׂרָפִים וּשְׂעִירִים הַנִּשְׂרָפִים שְׁחִיטָתָן בַּצָּפוֹן,
chunks.en: The bulls that are burned and the goats that are burned are shechted in the north,
chunks.st: With regard to bulls that are burned and goats that are burned, their slaughter is in the north of the Temple courtyard,

chunks.en: and their blood is caught in a holy vessel in the north,
chunks.st: and the collection of their blood in a service vessel is in the north,

chunks.en: and their blood must be sprinkled on
chunks.st: and their blood requires sprinkling

chunks.en: the paroches and on the golden mizbeach.
chunks.st: upon the Curtain separating the Sanctuary and Holy of Holies, and upon the golden altar,

chunks.en: Each one of these puttings is a must.
chunks.st: and failure to perform even one placement of their blood disqualifies the offering.

chunks.en: The leftover blood he would pour on
chunks.st: As for the remainder of the blood that is left after those sprinklings, a priest would pour

chunks.en: the western base of the outer mizbeach.
chunks.st: it onto the western base of the external altar,

chunks.en: If he did not put it there,
chunks.st: but if he did not pour

chunks.en: it does not hold it back.
chunks.st: the remainder it does not disqualify the offering.

chunks.en: Both these and those are burned in the place of the ashes.
chunks.st: These, the bull and the goat of Yom Kippur, and those, the bulls and the goats that are burned, are then burned in the place of the ashes,
chunks.stMore: a place outside of Jerusalem where the priests would bring the ashes from the altar.

words.note: A place outside Yerushalayim where the ashes of the mizbeach were brought.

mishnayos.summary: The goats brought as a chatas for the whole Jewish people on Rosh Chodesh and Yom Tov are shechted in the north. Their blood is put on the four corners of the mizbeach, and male Kohanim eat them in the courtyard until midnight.

chunks.en: The chatas korbanos of the community and of one person:
chunks.st: These are the halakhot of the communal and the individual sin offerings.

chunks.en: These are the chatas korbanos of the community:
chunks.st: These are the communal sin offerings:

chunks.en: the goats of Rosh Chodesh and of the Yamim Tovim.
chunks.st: Goats of the New Moon and of the Festivals.

words.note: Rosh Chodesh.

chunks.en: They are shechted in the north,
chunks.st: Their slaughter is in the north of the Temple courtyard,

chunks.en: and their blood is caught in a holy vessel in the north,
chunks.st: and the collection of their blood in a service vessel is in the north,

chunks.en: and their blood needs four puttings
chunks.st: and their blood requires four placements

chunks.en: on the four corners.
chunks.st: on the four corners of the altar.

words.note: The four corners of the mizbeach.

chunks.en: How? He went up the ramp and turned to the ledge,
chunks.st: How did the priest do so? He ascended the ramp of the altar and turned right to the surrounding ledge and he continued east,

words.note: A narrow walkway around the mizbeach.

chunks.en: and came to the southeast corner,
chunks.st: and he came to the southeast corner

chunks.en: then the northeast,
chunks.st: and sprinkled the blood of the sin offering there and then to the northeast corner and sprinkled the blood there,

chunks.en: then the northwest,
chunks.st: and then to the northwest corner and sprinkled the blood there,

chunks.en: then the southwest.
chunks.st: and the southwest
chunks.stMore: corner, where he performed the fourth sprinkling and descended from the altar.

chunks.en: The leftover blood he would pour
chunks.st: He would pour the remainder of the blood

chunks.en: on the southern base.
chunks.st: on the southern base of the altar.

chunks.he: וְנֶאֱכָלִין לִפְנִים מִן הַקְּלָעִים לְזִכְרֵי כְהֻנָּה
chunks.en: And they are eaten inside the curtains by male Kohanim,
chunks.st: And the meat portions of the offering are eaten within the curtains, i.e., in the Temple courtyard, by the males of the priesthood.

words.note: Inside the courtyard of the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.he: בְּכָל מַאֲכָל לְיוֹם וָלַיְלָה עַד חֲצוֹת:
chunks.en: cooked any way, for a day and a night, until midnight.
chunks.st: And they are eaten prepared in any form of food preparation, on the day the offering is sacrificed and during the night that follows, until midnight.

mishnayos.summary: The olah is one of the holiest korbanos. It is shechted in the north, its blood is put on the mizbeach twice so it reaches all four sides, and it is skinned, cut up, and burned whole.

chunks.en: The olah is one of the holiest korbanos.
chunks.st: The burnt offering is an offering of the most sacred order.

chunks.en: It is shechted in the north,
chunks.st: Its slaughter is in the north

chunks.en: and its blood is caught in a holy vessel in the north,
chunks.st: of the Temple courtyard and the collection of its blood in a service vessel is in the north,

chunks.he: וְדָמָהּ טָעוּן שְׁתֵּי מַתָּנוֹת שֶׁהֵן אַרְבַּע,
chunks.en: and its blood needs two puttings that are four,
chunks.st: and its blood requires two placements that are four,

words.note: Put on two opposite corners so it reaches all four sides.

chunks.en: and it needs skinning, cutting up, and to be burned whole on the fire.
chunks.st: and it requires flaying of its carcass and the cutting of the sacrificial animal into pieces, and it is consumed in its entirety, with the exception of its hide, by the fire of the altar.

mishnayos.summary: The shelamim of the community and the different kinds of asham are shechted in the north. Male Kohanim eat them in the courtyard, cooked any way, until midnight.

chunks.en: The shelamim of the community, and the asham korbanos.
These are the asham korbanos:
the asham for stealing,

words.note: Brought by one who kept money that was not his and swore falsely.

chunks.en: the asham for using holy things,

words.note: Using something that belongs to Hashem by mistake.

chunks.en: the asham of the shifchah charufah,

words.note: A korban brought for a certain forbidden relationship.

chunks.en: the asham of a nazir,

words.note: Someone who promised not to drink wine or cut his hair for a time.

chunks.en: the asham of a metzora,
and the asham talui.

words.note: Brought when a person is not sure if he did a sin.

chunks.en: They are shechted in the north,
and their blood is caught in a holy vessel in the north,

chunks.he: וְדָמָן טָעוּן שְׁתֵּי מַתָּנוֹת שֶׁהֵן אַרְבַּע,
chunks.en: and their blood needs two puttings that are four,

chunks.he: וְנֶאֱכָלִין לִפְנִים מִן הַקְּלָעִים לְזִכְרֵי כְהֻנָּה
chunks.en: And they are eaten inside the curtains by male Kohanim,

chunks.he: בְּכָל מַאֲכָל לְיוֹם וָלַיְלָה עַד חֲצוֹת:
chunks.en: cooked any way, for a day and a night, until midnight.

mishnayos.summary: The todah and the nazir's ram are less holy korbanos. They may be shechted anywhere in the courtyard and eaten by anyone in all of Yerushalayim until midnight. The Kohen's portion may be eaten by his family too.

chunks.en: The todah and the ram of a nazir
chunks.st: The thanks offering and nazirite’s ram

words.note: A korban to thank Hashem after being saved.

chunks.en: are less holy korbanos.
chunks.st: are offerings of lesser sanctity.

chunks.en: They are shechted anywhere in the courtyard,
chunks.st: Their slaughter is anywhere in the Temple courtyard,

chunks.he: וְדָמָן טָעוּן שְׁתֵּי מַתָּנוֹת שֶׁהֵן אַרְבַּע,
chunks.en: and their blood needs two puttings that are four,
chunks.st: and their blood requires two placements that are four,

chunks.en: and they are eaten in the whole city by anyone,
chunks.st: and they are eaten throughout the city of Jerusalem, by every person, i.e., any ritually pure Jew,

words.note: Yerushalayim.

chunks.en: cooked any way,
chunks.st: prepared in any manner of food preparation,

chunks.en: for a day and a night, until midnight.
chunks.st: on the day the offering was sacrificed and during the night that follows, until midnight.

chunks.en: The part taken off from them is like them,
chunks.st: The status of the portion that is separated from them and given to the priests is similar to theirs;

words.note: The portion given to the Kohen.

chunks.en: except that the part taken off is eaten by the Kohanim,
chunks.st: but the portion that is separated is eaten by the priests,

chunks.en: their wives, their children, and their servants.
chunks.st: by their wives, and by their children, and by their slaves.

mishnayos.summary: Shelamim are less holy korbanos. They may be shechted anywhere in the courtyard and eaten by anyone in all of Yerushalayim, for two days and one night.

chunks.en: Shelamim are less holy korbanos.
chunks.st: Peace offerings are offerings of lesser sanctity.

chunks.en: They are shechted anywhere in the courtyard,
chunks.st: Their slaughter is anywhere in the Temple courtyard,

chunks.he: וְדָמָן טָעוּן שְׁתֵּי מַתָּנוֹת שֶׁהֵן אַרְבַּע,
chunks.en: and their blood needs two puttings that are four,
chunks.st: and their blood requires two placements that are four,

chunks.en: and they are eaten in the whole city by anyone,
chunks.st: and they are eaten throughout the city of Jerusalem, by every person, i.e., any ritually pure Jew,

chunks.st: prepared in any manner of food preparation,

chunks.en: for two days and one night.
chunks.st: for two days and one night,

chunks.en: The part taken off from them is like them,
chunks.st: The status of the portion that is separated from them and given to the priests is similar to theirs;

chunks.en: except that the part taken off is eaten by the Kohanim,
chunks.st: but the portion that is separated is eaten by the priests,

chunks.en: their wives, their children, and their servants.
chunks.st: by their wives, and by their children, and by their slaves.

mishnayos.summary: The bechor, maaser and korban Pesach need only one putting of blood. The bechor is eaten by Kohanim and maaser by anyone, for two days. The korban Pesach is eaten only at night, until midnight, by those signed up for it, and only roasted.

chunks.en: The bechor, the maaser, and the korban Pesach
chunks.st: The firstborn offering, the animal tithe offering, and the Paschal offering

chunks.en: are less holy korbanos.
chunks.st: are offerings of lesser sanctity.

chunks.en: They are shechted anywhere in the courtyard,
chunks.st: Their slaughter is anywhere in the Temple courtyard,

chunks.en: and their blood needs one putting,
chunks.st: and their blood requires one placement,

chunks.en: as long as he puts it over the base.
chunks.st: provided that the priest places it so that the blood goes on the base of the altar.

chunks.en: Their eating is different:
chunks.st: The halakha differs with regard to their consumption.

chunks.en: the bechor is eaten by the Kohanim,
chunks.st: The firstborn offering is eaten by the priests,

chunks.en: and the maaser by anyone.
chunks.st: and the animal tithe offering is eaten by any person, i.e., any ritually pure Jew.

chunks.en: And they are eaten in the whole city, by anyone,
chunks.st: And they are eaten throughout the city of Jerusalem,

chunks.en: cooked any way,
chunks.st: prepared in any manner of food preparation,

chunks.en: for two days and one night.
chunks.st: for two days and one night.

chunks.en: The korban Pesach is eaten only at night,
chunks.st: The Paschal offering is eaten only at night,

chunks.en: and it is eaten only until midnight,
chunks.st: and it is eaten only until midnight,

chunks.en: and it is eaten only by those signed up for it,
chunks.st: and it is eaten only by its registrants,
chunks.stMore: i.e., those who registered in advance to partake of the offering,

words.en: by those signed up for it

chunks.en: and it is eaten only roasted.
chunks.st: and it is eaten only roasted, not prepared in any other manner.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Yosei says the holiest korbanos may be shechted on top of the mizbeach, as if it were the north side. The menachos had their kometz taken anywhere in the courtyard and were eaten by male Kohanim until midnight.

chunks.en: The holiest korbanos that were shechted on top of the mizbeach,
chunks.st: With regard to offerings of the most sacred order that one slaughtered atop the altar,

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: it is as if they were shechted in the north.
chunks.st: Their status is as though they were slaughtered in the north, and the offerings are therefore valid.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei the son of Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:

chunks.he: מֵחֲצִי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וְלַצָּפוֹן, כַּצָּפוֹן. מֵחֲצִי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וְלַדָּרוֹם,
chunks.en: from the middle of the mizbeach to the north is like the north; from the middle of the mizbeach to the south
chunks.st: The status of the area from the halfway point of the altar and to the south is like that of the south, and offerings of the most sacred order slaughtered in that area are therefore disqualified. The status of the area from the halfway point of the altar and to the north is like that of the north.

chunks.he: כַּדָּרוֹם. הַמְּנָחוֹת הָיוּ נִקְמָצוֹת בְּכָל מָקוֹם בָּעֲזָרָה,
chunks.en: is like the south. The menachos had their kometz taken anywhere in the courtyard,
chunks.st: Handfuls were removed from the meal offerings in any place in the Temple courtyard

chunks.he: וְנֶאֱכָלִין לִפְנִים מִן הַקְּלָעִים לְזִכְרֵי כְהֻנָּה,
chunks.en: and they are eaten inside the curtains by male Kohanim,
chunks.st: and were consumed within the area enclosed by the curtains by males of the priesthood,

chunks.en: cooked any way,
chunks.st: prepared in any form of food preparation that he chooses, e.g., roasted or boiled,

chunks.en: for a day and a night, until midnight.
chunks.st: for one day and night, until midnight.

mishnayos.stIntro: It was taught in the previous chapter that offerings of the most sacred order are to be slaughtered in the northern section of the Temple courtyard.

mishnayos.summary: The bird chatas was done at the southwest corner of the mizbeach. That corner was used for three things below the red line and three things above it.

chunks.en: The bird chatas was done
chunks.st: The sacrificial rite of a bird sin offering would be performed at

chunks.en: on the southwest corner.
chunks.st: the southwest corner of the altar.

chunks.en: Anywhere it was done, it was kosher,
chunks.st: And if its sacrificial rite was performed in any place on the altar, the offering was deemed valid;

chunks.en: but this was its place.
chunks.st: but that corner was its designated place.

chunks.en: And that corner was used for three things
chunks.st: And there were three matters

chunks.en: below,
chunks.st: for which the portion of that corner below the red line that served as the demarcation between the upper and lower portions of the altar served as the proper location,

chunks.en: and three above.
chunks.st: and there were three matters for which the portion of that corner above the red line served as their proper location.

chunks.he: מִלְּמַטָּן, חַטַּאת הָעוֹף וְהַהַגָּשׁוֹת וּשְׁיָרֵי הַדָּם.
chunks.en: Below: the bird chatas, bringing the menachos near, and the leftover blood.
chunks.st: The following rites were performed below the red line: Sacrificing a bird sin offering, and bringing meal offerings near the altar before removal of the handful, and pouring out the remaining blood.

words.note: Bringing a mincha up to the corner of the mizbeach before taking its kometz.

chunks.en: Above: pouring the water and the wine, and the olah

chunks.st: Just as the altar and the ramp sanctify

mishnayos.summary: A korban that comes more often goes first. So the tamid comes before the mussaf, and the mussaf of Shabbos comes before the mussaf of Rosh Chodesh.

chunks.en: Anything that is more frequent than another
chunks.st: Any offering that is more frequent than another

chunks.en: comes before the other.
chunks.st: precedes the other offering. Therefore,

chunks.en: The tamid korbanos come before the mussaf korbanos,
chunks.st: the daily offerings precede the additional offerings,
chunks.stMore: which are sacrificed only on certain days. When Shabbat and the New Moon coincide,

Extra korbanos brought on Shabbos and Yom Tov.

chunks.he: מוּסְפֵי שַׁבָּת קוֹדְמִין לְמוּסְפֵי רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ,

mishnayos.summary: A holier korban goes first. The mishnah lists the order: chatas, asham, todah and nazir's ram, shelamim, and bechor, and gives the reason for each one.

chunks.st: Any offering that is more sacred than another

chunks.en: comes before the other.
chunks.st: precedes the other

chunks.st: the blood of the sin offering precedes the blood of the burnt offering

chunks.en: because it brings forgiveness.
chunks.st: because it effects acceptance,
chunks.stMore: i.e., atonement, for severe transgressions punishable by karet. Likewise, if there are limbs of a burnt offering and portions of a sin offering to be burned on the altar,

chunks.en: Parts of an olah come before the fats of a chatas,
chunks.st: the burning of the limbs of the burnt offering precedes the portions of the sin offering,

chunks.en: because they are all burned in the fire.

chunks.en: because its blood is put on
chunks.st: due to the fact that its blood is placed on

chunks.st: A guilt offering precedes a thanks offering and the nazirite’s ram

chunks.en: because it is one of the holiest korbanos.
chunks.st: due to the fact that it is an offering of the most sacred order, and the others are offerings of lesser sanctity.

chunks.en: The todah and the nazir's ram come before shelamim,
chunks.st: A thanks offering and a nazirite’s ram precede a peace offering

chunks.st: due to the fact that they are eaten for one day,

chunks.st: and the thanks offering and nazirite’s ram require loaves

chunks.en: Shelamim come before a bechor,

mishnayos.summary: A bechor goes before maaser because it is holy from birth and eaten by Kohanim. Maaser goes before bird korbanos because it is shechted and has holiest parts, its blood and its fats.

chunks.he: הַבְּכוֹר קוֹדֵם לַמַּעֲשֵׂר מִפְּנֵי שֶׁקְּדֻשָּׁתוֹ מֵרֶחֶם,
chunks.en: The bechor comes before maaser because it is holy from birth,
chunks.st: The firstborn offering precedes the animal tithe offering because it is sanctified from the womb,

chunks.en: and it is eaten by the Kohanim.
chunks.st: and it is eaten by the priests, whereas everyone may partake of the animal tithe offering.

mishnayos.summary: Bird korbanos go before menachos because they have blood. A sinner's mincha goes before a mincha given as a gift, and a bird chatas goes before a bird olah.

chunks.en: Birds come before menachos,
chunks.st: The bird offerings precede meal offerings

chunks.en: because they are kinds with blood.
chunks.st: due to the fact that they are types whose blood is presented, and atonement is effected by the blood.

chunks.en: A sinner's mincha comes before a gift mincha,
chunks.st: The meal offering of a sinner precedes a voluntary meal offering

chunks.en: because it comes for a sin.
chunks.st: due to the fact that it comes to atone for a sin.

chunks.en: A bird chatas comes before a bird olah.
chunks.st: For the same reason the sacrifice of the bird sin offering precedes the sacrifice of the bird burnt offering,

chunks.en: And so too when setting it aside as holy.
chunks.st: and likewise with regard to its consecration, the sin offering takes precedence.

mishnayos.summary: Every chatas goes before every asham, except the asham of a metzora, which makes him ready to become tahor. Most asham korbanos are two-year-old rams worth two shekels, but those of a nazir and a metzora are one year old.

chunks.en: All the chatas korbanos in the Torah
chunks.st: All the sin offerings mandated by the Torah

chunks.st: take precedence over the guilt offerings, as explained in the previous mishna (89a),

chunks.en: except for the asham of a metzora,

chunks.en: because it comes to make him fit.
chunks.st: because it comes to render one fit.
chunks.stMore: One who has been cured of leprosy must undergo a process through which he is rendered ritually pure before coming into contact with consecrated items. Although he must also bring a sin offering, his guilt offering is more central to that process of purification and therefore it takes precedence over the sin offering.

words.note: It helps make the metzora tahor again.

chunks.en: All the asham korbanos in the Torah come as
chunks.st: All the guilt offerings mandated by the Torah come

chunks.en: two years old and come worth silver shekels,
chunks.st: as rams in their second year, and come worth two silver shekels,

words.note: Worth two silver shekels.

chunks.en: except for the asham of a nazir and the asham of a metzora,
chunks.st: except for the guilt offering of a nazirite and the guilt offering of a leper,

chunks.en: which come one year old
chunks.st: as they come from sheep in their first year,

chunks.en: and do not need to be worth silver shekels.
chunks.st: and do not need to come worth two silver shekels, as they have no fixed value.

mishnayos.summary: The holier korbanos are also eaten first. Rabbi Meir says yesterday's shelamim are eaten before today's chatas and asham; the Sages say the chatas goes first because it is one of the holiest korbanos.

chunks.en: Just as they come first in offering them,
chunks.st: Just as the more sacred offerings precede other offerings with regard to their sacrifice, as taught in the previous mishna (89a),

chunks.en: so they come first in eating them.
chunks.st: they also precede the others with regard to their consumption.

chunks.he: שְׁלָמִים שֶׁל אֶמֶשׁ וּשְׁלָמִים שֶׁל הַיּוֹם,

chunks.st: or a guilt offering from today,

chunks.en: because it is one of the holiest korbanos.
chunks.st: due to the fact that it is an offering of the most sacred order.
chunks.stMore: Likewise, the guilt offering precedes the peace offering, as it is also of the most sacred order.

chunks.en: And with all of them, the Kohanim may change how they eat them,

chunks.st: the priests are permitted to eat them roasted,

chunks.st: or boiled, or cooked,
